summary: Eastern Lane FPA lookouts on Laurel Mountain, Lane County OR: cabin built 1942, burned 1945 and rebuilt; all removed by 1979; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Series of towers: 1942 cab (on a 45-ft tree, or a seven-ft tower per another account), 1945 replacement (41 ft or 50 ft, sources differ), 25-ft treated timber tower from 1954
facts.status_note: All lookouts removed by 1979 per firetower.org and firelookout.com; no source describes what remains on the summit

access.note: No source describes public access to the summit today

events.note: Camp built in 1930 per firetower.org only; firelookout.com does not mention it
Cab atop a 45-ft tree (firetower.org, firelookout.com); Forest Lookouts gives a hip-roof cab on a seven-ft tower
Lookout cabin burned to the ground, March 1945, per a Forest Log item quoted on the Forest Lookouts site; cause not established
Replacement: planned 50-ft tower with 14x14 cabin and a 1945 live-in house on a 50-ft tower (Forest Lookouts); firetower.org says a 41-ft tower one mile west, firelookout.com says half a mile west

Mary Bea Hall, an 18-year-old University of Oregon sophomore, reported fires from the lookout; the January 28, 1946 article says she had done the work for the last two summers and does not give the years
25-ft treated timber tower: L-4 flat tower (firetower.org), or with an ODF live-in cab on the summit (firelookout.com)
Registered March 25, 2011 as US 877, OR 244; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not settled: firetower.org and firelookout.com give a 41-ft tower built in 1945 (one mile or half a mile west), while Forest Lookouts quotes a 50-ft replacement plan. The story reports both.
firelookout.com gives about 11 miles south of Cottage Grove; the 1945 Forest Log item quoted on Forest Lookouts gives about 20 miles. Not resolved; the story reports both.
firetower.org gives 3,350 ft (1,021 m) and firelookout.com gives 3301 ft. The brief's 1021.1 m follows firetower.org and is kept.

notes_for_editor: Height_m from the brief (15.2 m, 50 ft) matches only the 50-ft plan; left out of facts because the sources describe 41-ft, 50-ft and 25-ft towers. No source describes the summit today, so access is unknown. Two web searches turned up nothing on Laurel Mountain. Forest Lookouts quotes The Forest Log and a district annual report secondhand. The statement that no source describes the site today is unfooted by design.
